speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the underlying cause, please tell me: how old are you, and when did your growth spurt peak?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Lipoid CAH). The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly, labial fusion), maternal hirsutism during pregnancy, and current virilization (severe acne) in an adolescent with bone fragility indicates a 21-hydroxylase deficiency affecting both adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis.
